newsitem.title: POLAND: Merrill Lynch downgrades Slaski to neutral.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch downgrades Slaski to neutral.

text.p: Merrill Lynch downgraded Polish Bank Slaski SA long-term rating to neutral from buy because of the stock's 33 percent appreciation in the last two months, Merrill Lynch said in a report dated January 22.
Merrill Lynch said its dividend discount model showed that Slaski's shares exceeded fair value by 12 percent and P/NAV model showed Slaski shares were overvalued by 50 percent.
It said it saw Slaski trading at P/E ratio of 8.5 in 1997 but said its long-term fundamental prospects could support the 33-percent premium to their five-bank 1997 average P/E of 6.4.

"We maintain a neutral intermediate-term opinion...first of all the static nature of this model (the P/NAV) overlooks the above average growth prospects of the Polish banks and finds all five of the Polish banks which we follow overvalued by 15 to 50 percent," it said.
